purpose: Recorded numerical candidates for balancing the three already dimensionless P418 full-coupled training groups: state data, face mass flux data and eight-equation physics.

physical_parameter_status.statement: These are neural-network optimisation settings. They do not alter pebble-bed geometry, helium properties, Li4SiO4 properties, heating, boundary conditions or any other physical input.

official_implementation_constants.source: Bischof and Kraus official repository src/update_rules.py at commit b3c76d2bed7c6bebb2e2628575008a04858472cf
official_implementation_constants.role: Numerical protection against a zero relative-loss denominator; not a physical parameter.

primary_sources.paper: Multi-Objective Loss Balancing for Physics-Informed Deep Learning
primary_sources.authors: Rafael Bischof and Michael A. Kraus
primary_sources.journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 439 (2025) 117914

primary_sources.paper: Understanding and mitigating gradient pathologies in physics-informed neural networks
primary_sources.authors: Sifan Wang, Yujun Teng and Paris Perdikaris
primary_sources.role_here: Physical reason for checking loss-gradient imbalance; not selected as the first implemented candidate because it requires additional full-gradient statistics.

primary_sources.paper: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
primary_sources.authors: Zhao Chen, Vijay Badrinarayanan, Chen-Yu Lee and Andrew Rabinovich
primary_sources.role_here: Mature comparison method reviewed by the ReLoBRaLo paper; not the first implementation because it adds a separate gradient-norm optimisation.

formal_candidates.source: Neutral equal-weight baseline after training-only dimensional scaling and within-group averaging.
Bischof and Kraus, arXiv:2110.09813, table VIII, Burgers setting.
Bischof and Kraus, arXiv:2110.09813, table VIII, Kirchhoff setting.
Bischof and Kraus, arXiv:2110.09813, table VIII, Helmholtz setting.

selection_protocol.checkpoint_selection: Arithmetic mean of the three dimensionless validation loss groups. This score is independent of the adaptive training weights.
selection_protocol.method_selection: Compare the four recorded candidates on validation curves only, using the same architecture, split and random seed.
selection_protocol.independent_test: Read once after the weighting method and checkpoint are fixed.
selection_protocol.claim_limit: A published benchmark setting is only a candidate for this coupled pebble-bed problem. Superiority is not claimed before the formal validation comparison is complete.
